The method manufactures a three-dimensional shaped object by repeatedly and alternately forming powder layers and solidified layers. In this process, a layer of powder is first spread to a predetermined thickness, and selected portions of that powder layer are then irradiated with a light beam. The irradiated portions are sintered or melted and subsequently solidified, thereby forming a solidified layer corresponding to a desired cross-sectional shape of the object. By repeating the formation of powder layers and the selective irradiation and solidification steps, the solidified layers are stacked one upon another to produce the final three-dimensional shaped object.

The three-dimensional shaped object produced by this method is particularly suitable for use as a metal mold. In order to improve heat removal properties during molding, the object is formed with an internal flow path through which a cooling medium, such as water or another coolant, can flow. This cooling flow path is provided inside the body of the metal mold so that heat generated or transferred during molding can be efficiently removed.

A distinctive feature of the shaped object is that at least a part of the contour surface of the internal cooling flow path has substantially the same shape as the concavity-convexity surface of the three-dimensional shaped object. In other words, the cooling flow path may follow the uneven external or molding surface of the object, including its recessed and protruding portions. As a result, the cooling medium can be guided along a path that closely corresponds to the shape of the mold surface, allowing more uniform and efficient cooling. This configuration enhances the heat removal performance of the metal mold and can contribute to improved molding accuracy, reduced cycle time, and better quality of molded products.
outputs.L4:
A method is provided for manufacturing a three-dimensional metal mold using an additive manufacturing process in which metal powder is deposited in successive layers and selectively solidified by irradiation with a light beam, such as a laser beam or electron beam. In this method, a thin layer of metal powder is first spread over a forming surface. A predetermined region of the powder layer, corresponding to a cross-sectional shape of the mold to be produced, is then selectively sintered or melted by the light beam. After solidification of that region, another powder layer is formed on top of the previously solidified layer, and the selective sintering or melting step is repeated. By successively laminating and solidifying these layers, a three-dimensional metal mold having a desired external and internal structure is produced.

The mold formed by this method includes, within its body, one or more flow paths for a cooling medium such as water, oil, air, or another temperature-control fluid. These cooling-media flow paths are formed at the same time as the mold body during the layer-by-layer manufacturing process, rather than being drilled or machined afterward. As a result, the cooling paths can be given complex shapes that would be difficult or impossible to obtain using conventional machining techniques.

The molding surface of the metal mold includes a concave-convex shape, such as grooves, projections, recesses, ribs, textured regions, or other uneven surface portions. At least a portion of the contour of the internal cooling-media flow path is formed so as to correspond to, follow, or approximate the shape of this concave-convex molding surface. In other words, the cooling path is arranged not merely as a straight or simple passage inside the mold, but is shaped so that it runs close to and along the uneven surface profile of the mold.

Because the cooling-media flow path follows the contour of the concave-convex surface, the distance between the molding surface and the cooling passage can be made more uniform, even in regions where the surface has projections or recesses. This improves the removal of heat from the molding surface during use of the mold. In particular, heat can be efficiently extracted from portions that would otherwise be difficult to cool, such as raised portions, deeply recessed portions, or areas having abrupt changes in surface geometry.

The resulting three-dimensional metal mold therefore provides enhanced cooling performance compared with a mold having conventional straight cooling channels. Improved heat removal can shorten molding cycle time, reduce temperature variation across the molding surface, improve dimensional accuracy of molded products, and reduce defects caused by uneven cooling. The method also allows the cooling structure and the surface geometry of the mold to be designed together, enabling the production of molds with complex surface shapes and highly efficient internal temperature-control passages.

**In Order To**

The phrase **“in order to”** is commonly used to explain the purpose or reason for an action. It means **“so that something can happen”** or **“for the purpose of.”** This phrase is often used in formal writing, academic texts, business communication, and everyday speech.

For example, a person might say, **“I study every day in order to improve my knowledge.”** This means that the reason for studying every day is to gain more knowledge. Another example is, **“Companies use advertising in order to attract more customers.”** Here, the purpose of advertising is to increase customer interest.

Using **“in order to”** helps make sentences clear because it shows the connection between an action and its goal. It is especially useful when explaining plans, intentions, or reasons. However, in many cases, it can be replaced by the shorter word **“to.”** For example, **“She exercises to stay healthy”** has the same meaning as **“She exercises in order to stay healthy.”**

In conclusion, **“in order to”** is an important phrase for expressing purpose. It helps writers and speakers explain why something is done and what result they hope to achieve.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style summary for a method of manufacturing a 3D shaped object by powder bed fusion, including cooling media flow paths and a concave-convex surface for improved heat removal in a metal mold.
counterfactuals.output:
A method of manufacturing a three-dimensional shaped object by powder bed fusion is provided. The method includes forming, in a layer-by-layer manner, a metal mold or mold insert having an internal cooling structure configured to remove heat from a molding surface. A powder material is spread to form a powder layer, selected regions of the powder layer are irradiated with an energy beam to melt or sinter the powder material, and the steps are repeated to build the three-dimensional shaped object.

The three-dimensional shaped object includes a cavity surface or other heat-receiving surface, a plurality of cooling media flow paths disposed inside the object, and a concave-convex surface formed between the heat-receiving surface and the cooling media flow paths. The cooling media flow paths are configured to allow passage of a cooling medium, such as water, oil, air, or another heat-transfer fluid. The concave-convex surface may include projections, recesses, fins, ribs, grooves, corrugations, undulations, or combinations thereof, thereby increasing a heat-transfer area and promoting heat conduction from the molding surface toward the cooling media flow paths.

In one embodiment, the cooling media flow paths are formed conformally with respect to the contour of the molding surface and are arranged at a substantially uniform distance from the molding surface. The concave-convex surface may be provided on an outer wall of the cooling media flow path, on an inner wall of the cooling media flow path, or in a region interposed between the molding surface and the cooling media flow path. The concave-convex surface may be integrally formed during the powder bed fusion process, thereby eliminating or reducing a need for post-machining of internal heat-transfer structures.

The method may further include determining, based on thermal analysis data, a location, shape, pitch, height, or depth of the concave-convex surface and a layout of the cooling media flow paths so as to improve heat removal from portions of the metal mold that are subject to elevated thermal loads. During manufacture, unfused powder may be removed from the cooling media flow paths through inlet and outlet openings formed in the object.

Accordingly, the manufactured metal mold provides improved cooling performance by increasing the surface area for heat exchange and by positioning cooling channels close to the molding surface in a shape that follows the three-dimensional geometry of the mold. This enables reduction of molding cycle time, suppression of local temperature rise, improvement of molded product quality, and extension of service life of the metal mold.

counterfactuals.output: An additive manufacturing method for producing a metal mold includes repeatedly forming layers of metal powder and selectively irradiating the layers with a laser beam to sinter or melt the powder, thereby successively building a mold body. The mold body includes an external molding surface having an uneven contour and an internal cooling channel formed integrally within the mold body during the layer-by-layer build process. The cooling channel extends along the molding surface and has a channel contour corresponding to, or substantially matching, the uneven contour of the external molding surface, thereby maintaining a reduced and substantially uniform distance between the cooling channel and the molding surface. The method enables formation of a conformal cooling structure that would be difficult or impossible to manufacture by conventional drilling, improving cooling efficiency, temperature uniformity, and molding cycle time.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a Japanese patent translation-style description of a manufacturing method for a three-dimensional shaped object with improved cooling properties, made by alternately forming powder layers and solidified layers.
counterfactuals.output:
【発明の名称】  
冷却特性に優れた三次元造形物の製造方法

【技術分野】  
本発明は、粉末層の形成と該粉末層の選択的な固化とを交互に繰り返すことにより三次元造形物を製造する方法に関し、特に、内部に冷却媒体流路、放熱構造又は熱伝導性向上部を有する三次元造形物を高精度に製造する方法に関する。

【背景技術】  
従来、金属粉末又は樹脂粉末を層状に敷き詰め、レーザビーム、電子ビーム等のエネルギービームを照射して所望領域を溶融又は焼結させることにより固化層を形成し、これを積層することで三次元造形物を製造する積層造形法が知られている。  
このような方法によれば、切削加工では形成が困難な複雑形状、例えば内部流路、格子構造、フィン構造等を有する造形物を製造することができる。

しかしながら、従来の積層造形物においては、内部に冷却用流路を形成した場合であっても、流路壁面の粗さ、未溶融粉末の残留、熱伝導経路の不連続性等に起因して、十分な冷却性能が得られない場合があった。また、造形中の熱蓄積により、冷却流路近傍に変形、割れ、又は密度低下が生じることがあり、冷却性能及び機械的強度の両立が困難であった。

【発明の概要】  
本発明は、粉末層及び固化層を交互に形成して三次元造形物を製造する際に、冷却媒体の流通性及び熱伝導性を向上させることにより、冷却特性に優れた三次元造形物を得ることを目的とする。

本発明の一態様に係る三次元造形物の製造方法は、  
造形テーブル上又は既形成の固化層上に粉末材料を供給して粉末層を形成する粉末層形成工程と、  
前記粉末層のうち三次元造形物の断面形状に対応する領域にエネルギービームを照射して固化層を形成する固化層形成工程と、  
前記粉末層形成工程及び前記固化層形成工程を交互に繰り返す積層工程と、  
を含み、  
前記固化層形成工程において、造形物内部に冷却媒体を流通させるための冷却流路を形成する非固化領域を残存させるとともに、該冷却流路の周囲に、母材部よりも高密度又は高熱伝導性を有する冷却促進部を形成することを特徴とする。

【発明の効果】  
本発明によれば、三次元造形物内部に所望形状の冷却流路を形成しつつ、該冷却流路の周囲に熱伝導性に優れた冷却促進部を形成できるため、発熱部から冷却媒体への熱移動を効率化することができる。  
また、冷却流路の壁面を緻密化又は平滑化することにより、冷却媒体の圧力損失を低減し、未固化粉末の残留を抑制できる。  
さらに、造形中の照射条件を冷却流路近傍と他の領域とで異ならせることにより、変形及び割れの発生を抑制しつつ、高い冷却性能を有する三次元造形物を得ることができる。

【発明を実施するための形態】  
以下、本発明の実施形態について説明する。

本実施形態に係る製造方法では、まず、金属粉末を造形チャンバ内の造形テーブル上に供給し、リコータ又はローラにより所定厚さの粉末層を形成する。粉末材料としては、例えば、マルエージング鋼、ステンレス鋼、工具鋼、チタン合金、アルミニウム合金、銅合金、ニッケル基合金等を用いることができる。冷却特性を重視する場合には、銅又は銅合金を含む粉末、あるいは銅系粉末と鉄系又はニッケル系粉末との混合粉末を用いてもよい。

次いで、レーザビーム又は電子ビームを粉末層に選択的に照射し、所定領域の粉末を溶融又は焼結させて固化層を形成する。このとき、造形データに基づいて、造形物の外殻部、内部母材部、冷却流路壁部及び冷却促進部をそれぞれ異なる照射条件で形成することが好ましい。

例えば、冷却流路壁部には、母材部よりも高いエネルギー密度でビームを照射することにより、相対密度の高い緻密層を形成する。これにより、冷却媒体が流通する流路壁面の気孔率を低減し、漏れの発生を抑制できる。また、ビーム走査ピッチを小さくする、再溶融走査を行う、又は輪郭走査を複数回実施することにより、冷却流路の内壁面を平滑化することができる。

一方、冷却流路の内部となる領域にはエネルギービームを照射せず、非固化粉末を残存させる。積層完了後、該非固化粉末を冷却流路の開口部から吸引、加圧気体、振動、超音波又は洗浄液により除去することで、冷却媒体を流通可能な中空流路が形成される。

冷却流路は、直線状に限られず、湾曲状、螺旋状、分岐状、合流状、蛇行状又は三次元的なネットワーク状であってもよい。また、冷却流路の断面形状は、円形、楕円形、長円形、多角形、涙滴形又はこれらの組合せであってもよい。特に、粉末除去性及び流体抵抗の観点から、冷却流路の下面側に過度なオーバーハングを有しない断面形状とすることが好ましい。

冷却促進部は、冷却流路の外周側、発熱部に対向する側、又は発熱部と冷却流路との間に形成される。冷却促進部は、例えば、母材部よりも高い熱伝導率を有する材料からなる領域、母材部よりも高密度に固化された領域、又は多数の微細フィン若しくは格子を含む領域として形成される。  
粉末材料が単一材料である場合には、冷却促進部におけるレーザ出力、走査速度、走査ピッチ又は積層厚さを調整することにより、空孔率を低減し、熱伝導経路を連続化することができる。  
一方、複数材料の供給が可能な装置を用いる場合には、冷却促進部に銅系粉末、アルミニウム系粉末又は高熱伝導性複合粉末を選択的に供給し、これを固化することにより、母材部よりも高熱伝導性の領域を形成してもよい。

さらに、冷却流路の内壁には、造形と同時に又は造形後に、乱流促進部を設けることができる。乱流促進部は、例えば、リブ、突起、螺旋溝、ディンプル又は微細凹凸からなる。これにより、冷却媒体と流路壁面との熱交換が促進され、冷却効率が向上する。乱流促進部は、圧力損失が過大とならない範囲で、冷却流路の一部、特に発熱量の大きい領域に対応する部分に設けることが好ましい。

積層工程においては、各層ごとに粉末層形成工程及び固化層形成工程を繰り返す。これにより、内部に冷却流路及び冷却促進部を有する三次元造形物が一体的に形成される。造形中には、造形テーブル又は造形チャンバを予熱してもよく、また、固化層形成後に局所的な再加熱又は応力緩和走査を行ってもよい。これにより、冷却流路周辺における残留応力及び反りを低減できる。

積層完了後、造形物を造形テーブルから分離し、冷却流路内に残留した非固化粉末を除去する。粉末除去後、必要に応じて、熱処理、熱間等方圧加圧処理、ショットピーニング、化学研磨、電解研磨、流体研磨又はめっき処理を施すことができる。特に、冷却流路内面に対して流体研磨又は化学研磨を行うことにより、内壁面粗さを低減し、冷却媒体の流動抵抗をさらに低減できる。

【実施例】  
一例として、金属粉末として銅合金粉末を用い、積層厚さを２０～６０μｍとし、各粉末層に対してファイバレーザを選択的に照射した。冷却流路壁部には、母材部よりも小さい走査ピッチ及び低い走査速度を適用し、輪郭走査を２回実施した。冷却流路の内部領域にはレーザを照射せず、非固化粉末を残した。  
積層後、冷却流路内の非固化粉末を圧縮空気及び超音波振動により除去した。その結果、三次元的に湾曲した冷却流路と、該冷却流路の周囲に形成された高密度の冷却促進部とを備える三次元造形物が得られた。得られた造形物は、同一外形で内部冷却流路を有しない造形物に比べて、発熱部近傍の温度上昇が低減され、冷却応答性が向上した。

【産業上の利用可能性】  
本発明に係る製造方法は、金型、射出成形用金型、ダイカスト金型、熱交換器、電子部品用放熱部材、航空機部品、自動車部品、半導体製造装置用部材、医療機器部材等、内部冷却性能又は放熱性能が要求される各種三次元造形物の製造に好適に利用することができる。

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal patent language, a powder-bed additive manufacturing process in which a 3D object is formed with internal coolant passages and a concavity-convexity surface having the same shape as part of the coolant path contour.
counterfactuals.output:
In one embodiment, a three-dimensional article is manufactured by a powder-bed additive manufacturing process. The process comprises providing a digital model of the article, the digital model defining an outer surface of the article, at least one internal coolant passage extending within the article, and a concavity-convexity surface formed on at least a portion of the article. The concavity-convexity surface is shaped so as to have a profile corresponding to, or substantially the same as, at least a portion of a contour of the internal coolant passage.

A layer of powder material is supplied onto a build platform and selectively irradiated with an energy beam in accordance with slice data generated from the digital model, thereby selectively melting or sintering the powder material to form a solidified layer. Thereafter, additional layers of powder material are successively supplied and selectively irradiated so as to form successive solidified layers integrally bonded to one another. By repeating the layer forming step, the three-dimensional article is built up while simultaneously forming the internal coolant passage within the article and the concavity-convexity surface on the article.

The internal coolant passage may be formed by leaving unsolidified powder in a region corresponding to the coolant passage during the selective irradiation step and subsequently removing the unsolidified powder from the article. The concavity-convexity surface may include alternating recessed portions and projecting portions, and at least one of the recessed portions or projecting portions may extend along a shape that corresponds to a curved, bent, branched, or serpentine contour of the internal coolant passage. In this manner, an external or accessible surface feature is provided which indicates, follows, or corresponds to the geometry of the internal coolant passage formed inside the article.

In certain embodiments, the concavity-convexity surface is formed directly above, adjacent to, or along a wall defining the coolant passage, such that the shape of the concavity-convexity surface conforms to a partial contour of the coolant passage. The concavity-convexity surface may thereby function as a surface identification feature, a heat-transfer enhancement feature, a stress-relief feature, a machining reference, or a structural feature corresponding to the internal coolant path.

The powder material may comprise a metal powder, including a nickel-based alloy, cobalt-based alloy, titanium alloy, aluminum alloy, stainless steel, or other heat-resistant alloy. The energy beam may comprise a laser beam or an electron beam. The additive manufacturing process may be selective laser melting, selective laser sintering, direct metal laser sintering, laser powder-bed fusion, or electron-beam powder-bed fusion.

Thus, the article is formed as a monolithic additively manufactured body including an internal coolant passage and a concavity-convexity surface having substantially the same shape as at least a portion of the contour of the coolant passage, without requiring separate assembly of the coolant passage or post-formation attachment of the concavity-convexity surface.
